_comment: Scripted FakeLlmProvider output for the SINGLE-job fit rating (src/lib/fit/rate.ts) of alex-chen against stripe-sbe — the match_rating check on the application page. The `match` key is load-bearing, not decoration: llm/rate-batch.json is already an unguarded 'rate' fixture, and pickScript (src/lib/testmode/llm.ts) throws when two unguarded fixtures claim one promptKind. The string is the literal first line of rateFitMessage() in src/lib/llm/prompts/fit.ts for this job, so it appears in the batch prompt's text only when this exact job is the one being rated. Honest-AI invariant, enforced by reading this file: a tier and reasons, and not one number, percentage, score or grade anywhere. The third reason is a gap — it cites nothing, because the evidence for an absence is an absence.
match: Job: Senior Backend Engineer at Stripe

reasons.text: The posting is about keeping the charge path up; Alex already owns a production ledger that settles card transactions across three processors, which is that job under a different company's name.
Stripe asks for idempotent, exactly-once processing over Kafka. Alex designed idempotent retry semantics for webhook ingestion and moved six services onto a Kafka event bus.
Nothing in the résumé mentions gRPC or service meshes, which the posting lists under what it is looking for. That is a real gap to be ready to talk about.
